message:
## Root cause: duplicate charges on retry

The race was between the payment worker and the retry cron — both could pick up the same pending order if the retry fired within the same second as the original attempt, since neither held a lock on the order row.

Fixed by adding a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` around the charge attempt and an idempotency key derived from the order ID and attempt number. Ran 500 concurrent requests against the same order in a load test afterward — exactly one charge went through every time, no duplicates.
note: Detailed root cause plus load-test verification with concurrency.

message:
## Duplicate rows in the daily orders export

Root cause was a missing dedup key in the merge step — when the source system retried a batch after a timeout, the pipeline treated the retried rows as new instead of recognizing them as the same orders.

Added the natural key (order_id, updated_at) to the merge condition and backfilled the last 30 days. Compared row counts against the source system for each of those 30 days afterward and every day now matches exactly.
note: Root cause plus backfill plus row-count reconciliation.
